title: CondoGuard Midterm Endorsement Rules
content:
Endorsement provisions of the CondoGuard Unit-Owners Policy for midterm changes: adding or removing an optional coverage, and changing a limit, the deductible or the occupancy.

## A. When an endorsement may be made

A1. Endorsements are added or removed only while the policy is bound, in force or pending nonrenewal, as the policy record shows.

A2. *Retired clause.* "A midterm change takes effect no earlier than the date the named insured requests it and before the expiration date." This clause is no longer in force for a liability raise, adding a unit rental endorsement, a Coverage A realignment or a deductible raise; each of those changes is governed by its own current effective-date rule. For every other midterm change, removing a unit rental endorsement among them, it is in force: the change takes effect no earlier than the date the named insured requests it, and before the expiration date of the policy.

A3. Coverage increases are not accepted while the policy has a claim that has been reported and not closed, as the claim records show.

## B. What may be endorsed

B1. The loss assessment increase and water backup are bought in steps of 5000 USD above the tier's included limit, up to the tier's highest total loss assessment limit or highest total water backup limit; the endorsement records the new total.

B2. The unit rental endorsement is available only where the tier allows a unit rented to others to be insured with it, and it sets the occupancy to rented to others. The identity fraud endorsement is available only where the tier's included identity fraud limit is 0.

B3. A Coverage A change keeps Coverage A at or above the tier's minimum for the current master policy type and at or below the tier's maximum Coverage A; a Coverage C change keeps Coverage C within the tier's minimum and maximum Coverage C; a liability change lands on one of the tier's liability limits; a deductible change lands on one of the tier's deductible options.

B4. The deductible assessment sublimit is fixed by tier and can never be raised by endorsement, and coverages included in the package can never be removed.

B5. While the customer holds a live Larkspur Personal Umbrella Policy that schedules this policy as underlying, the liability limit is never lowered below the umbrella's required underlying condominium liability limit.

## C. Annual premium change

C1. The annual premium change is: for a loss assessment increase or water backup, the tier's rate per 5,000 USD for each step of 5000 USD, that is the rate multiplied by the difference between the new total and the current limit (taken as a positive amount), divided by 5000; for the identity fraud endorsement, the tier's identity fraud annual premium.

C2. *Retired clauses.* The following pieces of the annual premium change rule are no longer in force for the change named, which is governed by its current basis: the liability step premium per step along the tier's liability limits, for a liability raise; the tier's unit rental annual premium, for adding a unit rental endorsement; the Coverage A or Coverage C rate per 1,000 USD of change, for a Coverage A realignment; and, for a deductible change, the term premium multiplied by the new deductible's credit factor less the old deductible's credit factor, for a deductible raise. For other changes they remain in force: the liability step premium per step along the tier's liability limits for any other liability change, the tier's unit rental annual premium for removing a unit rental endorsement, the Coverage A or Coverage C rate per 1,000 USD of change for any other Coverage A change and for a Coverage C change (the rate multiplied by the difference between the new and the current limit, taken as a positive amount, divided by 1000), and, for any other deductible change, the term premium multiplied by the new deductible's credit factor less the old deductible's credit factor, using the factors below.

| Deductible (USD) | Credit factor |
|---|---|
| 500 | 0.05 |
| 1000 | 0.00 |
| 2500 | negative 0.10 |
| 5000 | negative 0.17 |

## D. Prorated premium and direction

D1. *Retired clause.* "The prorated premium is the annual change multiplied by the calendar days from the change effective date to the expiration date and divided by the calendar days in the term, rounded half-up to the cent" is no longer in force for a liability raise, adding a unit rental endorsement, a Coverage A realignment or a deductible raise, each of which is governed by its current basis. For other midterm changes, removing a unit rental endorsement among them, it is in force as written.

D2. The premium direction is additional for an increase, return for a decrease, and none when the prorated premium is below the tier's minimum premium change.

## E. Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A loss assessment limit raised from 5000 USD to 15000 USD on a tier whose rate is 8.00 USD per 5,000 USD: 8.00 multiplied by 10000 and divided by 5000 is an annual change of 16.00 USD. With 200 of 365 days left, the prorated premium is 16.00 multiplied by 200 and divided by 365, 8.767, rounded to 8.77 USD; on a tier whose minimum premium change is 5.00 USD it is not below the minimum, and the direction is additional. A deductible lowered from 1000 USD to 500 USD on a term premium of 800.00 USD changes the annual premium by 800.00 multiplied by 0.05 less 0.00, that is 40.00 USD, an increase. A unit rental endorsement removed on a tier whose unit rental annual premium is 76.00 USD changes the annual premium by 76.00 USD, a decrease; with 146 of 365 days left the prorated premium is 76.00 multiplied by 146 and divided by 365, 30.40 USD, and the direction is return.
